_coverage_rationale: REF-DU-1: PDF-only B2B SaaS deal (SynthCommerce) used as the canonical example for the deal understanding audit system. Exercises all five check layers: fidelity, understanding, usefulness, hallucination, and completeness.

ground_truth.what_company_does: B2B SaaS platform that helps mid-market e-commerce retailers optimize paid ad spend using first-party customer data signals and real-time attribution recalculation.
ground_truth.business_model: B2B SaaS with annual subscription contracts. Customers connect their Shopify or WooCommerce store and ad platforms. Revenue recognised on subscription start date. No usage-based fees.
ground_truth.revenue_model: Annual recurring subscription with three tiers: Starter $12K/yr, Growth $36K/yr, Enterprise custom pricing. No per-seat or usage fees. Primarily annual contracts with auto-renew.
ground_truth.go_to_market: Product-led growth via Shopify App Store and WooCommerce marketplace listings. Supplemented by direct outbound to merchants with >$5M GMV. No paid acquisition. Word-of-mouth from high NPS.
ground_truth.target_customer: Mid-market e-commerce brands with $2M–$50M GMV. Primary buyer is Head of Marketing or DTC Growth Lead. Core pain point is rising CAC from third-party cookie deprecation.
ground_truth.traction_summary: 280 paying customers, $1.2M ARR, 18% MoM growth over last 6 months, NPS 72, <2% monthly churn. Top 10 customers represent 45% of ARR.
ground_truth.market_positioning: Competes directly with Northbeam and Triple Whale in e-commerce attribution. Differentiates on real-time attribution recalculation — incumbents update overnight. Also supports headless commerce storefronts that competitors cannot instrument.
ground_truth.competitive_differentiation: Real-time attribution refresh versus overnight batch updates from Northbeam and Triple Whale. Native headless commerce support (competitors Shopify-only). First-party signals from all store events, not only purchase events.
key_strengths: Product-led growth via Shopify App Store eliminates need for enterprise sales motion — CAC near zero.
NPS 72 and <2% monthly churn demonstrate strong retention in a market with historically high SMB churn.
Real-time attribution is a genuine technical differentiator versus the two category incumbents.
Founder has prior experience building attribution tooling at Criteo.
key_risks: Distribution concentrated in Shopify App Store — a policy change or delisting could eliminate the PLG channel overnight.
ARR concentration: top 10 customers represent 45% of ARR, creating revenue cliff risk.
Attribution accuracy degrades with continued browser and OS privacy changes — mitigated but not eliminated.
Two well-funded incumbents (Northbeam, Triple Whale) could replicate real-time refresh within 12–18 months.
investor_relevance_notes: PLG motion with Shopify App Store is replicable and proven — key diligence question is growth rate post App Store saturation.
Funding ask ($3M seed) vs ARR ($1.2M) implies ~2.5x ARR valuation multiple — aggressive for current market.
Founder's Criteo background is credible signal for attribution accuracy claims — verify via reference check.

validation._note: Checks run against the output of GET /api/v1/deals/{deal_id}/understanding. TODO (DDA-UNDERSTANDING): implement the endpoint before live-deal checks become active.

understanding_checks.label: what_company_does captures ad-tech / attribution context
understanding_checks.note: A generic 'SaaS company for retailers' extract fails this — must reflect the specific attribution function.

understanding_checks.label: traction_summary contains key metrics (ARR or customer count)
understanding_checks.note: Numeric specificity is required — a vague 'strong growth' fails.

understanding_checks.label: go_to_market identifies Shopify App Store or PLG channel
understanding_checks.note: The PLG / zero-CAC motion is a key investor signal — vague 'online marketing' fails.

understanding_checks.label: competitive_differentiation names at least one incumbent
understanding_checks.note: Named competitor required — 'better than competition' is generic and fails.

understanding_checks.label: what_company_does is specific (not generic boilerplate)
understanding_checks.note: Boilerplate phrasing without domain-specific language signals hallucination or shallow extraction.

understanding_checks.label: what_company_does has minimum specificity (≥12 words)
understanding_checks.note: Sub-12-word descriptions are too shallow to be useful.

understanding_checks.label: revenue_model contains subscription / recurring language
understanding_checks.note: Must reflect the SaaS subscription structure — not transactional or usage-based language.

understanding_checks.label: business_model aligns with SaaS recurring revenue framing
understanding_checks.note: business_model and revenue_model should both use subscription/SaaS language.

understanding_checks.label: market_positioning mentions real-time attribution or specific differentiator
understanding_checks.note: Generic 'better performance' without the real-time angle misses the core positioning.

consistency_checks.label: business_model and revenue_model are both non-empty
consistency_checks.note: These two fields must both be populated — a missing one signals incomplete extraction.

consistency_checks.label: revenue_model and go_to_market share subscription / PLG alignment
consistency_checks.note: If revenue_model mentions annual contracts and go_to_market says 'Shopify App Store', at least one contract-related term should appear in both.

consistency_checks.label: traction_summary and target_customer mention same segment
consistency_checks.note: Traction figures must be attributed to the correct customer segment — not a different market.

hallucination_checks.label: what_company_does does not claim enterprise focus (company targets mid-market)
hallucination_checks.note: SynthCommerce explicitly targets mid-market — enterprise framing contradicts the source deck.

hallucination_checks.label: competitive_differentiation does not claim market monopoly / only player
hallucination_checks.note: Northbeam and Triple Whale are named competitors — 'only solution' claims are unsupported.

hallucination_checks.label: traction_summary does not claim profitability (company is pre-profit at seed stage)
hallucination_checks.note: No profitability data in the source deck — any profitability claim would be hallucinated.

hallucination_checks.label: revenue_model does not incorrectly claim usage-based or transactional pricing
hallucination_checks.note: SynthCommerce uses flat annual subscription tiers — usage-based framing is unsupported.
